units.translation: Λεγεβα-τυρ φρουρά πλέον καίουσα τῶν εἰρημένων [the watch is said to be burning more than the things mentioned], which is a feeble interpolation of a weak interpolator patching up as best he could a verse largely obliterated in the older book. Hesychius has preserved words worthy of Aeschylus, προσαιθρίζουσα πόμπιμον φλόγα [sending up the escorting flame]: πρὸς τὸν αἰθέρα ποιοῦσα [making it toward the ether], ὥστε ἄνω πέμπεσθαι τὴν φλόγα [so that the flame is sent upward], though he should rather have said ὥστε ἄνω φέρεσθαι τὴν πρὸς τὴν φρουράν πεπεμμένην φλόγα [so that the flame sent to the watch is borne upward]. On this see the Preface to the second Oxford edition p. VII, comparing two similar words whose knowledge we owe to Hesychius, Aeschylus's words οὐρανίζειν [to reach heaven] and προσαυρίζειν [to touch].
the watch sending up the escorting flame
the watch is said to be burning more than the things mentioned

in which it is easy to recognize this verse of Aeschylus, unless I am mistaken, νοτὶς προσαυρίζουσα χερσαία τροχή [the moisture touching the dry wheel]. Similar words of Aeschylus are προσαιθρίζειν [to send up] and οὐρανίζειν [to reach heaven], which see.
touching the dry wheel: the moisture falling upon the wheel by the breeze. It can also mean 'overtaking'; for ἐπαυρεῖν means to overtake and to hit upon.
